text:
sandeep: heads-up — brought up mercury12b-int4 on a tiny canary (3 pods) this morning. baseline fp16 -> int4 perf looks good (+12% throughput) but two pain points: (A) p95 jitter under sustained 8-10 batch assembly, (B) a small drop in summarization F1 (~0.9%). details below.

anna: drop the perf numbers + OOM logs? which quant method? symmetric/asymmetric?

sandeep: asym symmetric-per-tensor quant with percentile-clip 99.5. perf: p50 88ms -> 80ms, p95 360ms -> 330ms, tokens/sec +12%. summarization f1: fp16 0.611 -> int4 0.605. jitter trace: after ~4k requests free-list fragmentation increases and we see small alloc retries, sometimes slab reclaim that adds 40-80ms spikes. OOM snippet: 
```
[2025-01-06T14:12:05Z] CUDA OOM: alloc 768MB in slab_alloc.cc:198
  at redwood/runtime/allocator/slab_alloc.cc:198
  kv_cache resize -> attempt 2 -> fallback evict -> still fail
  prefetch worker pool exhausted
```

kevin: thanks. did you run with slot_reserve_fraction default? also what is prefetch_pool size?

sandeep: slot_reserve_fraction was 0.05, prefetch_pool default (8 threads). batch config: min 1, target 8, max 10. generation_window 128.

ciara: the F1 delta is small but needs triage. propose A/B: fp16 control vs int4 candidate w/ two variants: clip99.5 and clip98.0. Add regression benchmarks (summarize-long, dialogue-condense). If clip98 recovers F1 without perf hit, that might be the winner.

kevin: infra side — two quick mitigations: (1) increase slot_reserve_fraction to 0.14 for the canary, (2) reduce target_batch -> 5 to avoid sustained large assembly; (3) bump prefetch_pool to 16 and enable allocator compaction every 3 minutes (lightweight). Also add a soft batch cap in the serving runtime that refuses to form batch if freelist fragmentation > 0.4.

sandeep: good. i'll spin up two canary arms: int4-clip995 (target_batch 5, slot_reserve 14%, prefetch 16, compaction 3m) and int4-clip98 (same infra). launching now on 1% traffic.

allocator-bot: compaction job scheduled every 3m for canary group mercury12b-int4-canary. metrics hook: allocator_free_frag_ratio, oom_count, p95_latency.

anna: add a routing fallback: route to mercury12b-fp16 in same region on OOM, and to a lower-batch variant if frag ratio > 0.45. snippet: 
```json
{"fallback": {"on_oom": "mercury12b-fp16", "on_frag_gt": {"threshold": 0.45, "route": "mercury12b-int4-softbatch"}}}
```

ciara: also request a short quality bisect: run eval-suite only with single change clip->98 and measure hallucination-rate and compression ratio. keep the AB window 6h and rollback rule: F1 drop > 1.0% OR any OOM in canary window.

kevin: if fragmentation persists post compaction, next steps: (A) implement a freelist defragmenter that runs during low qps windows and compacts in-place, (B) consider switching to per-channel quant for critical attention layers only (hybrid quant), which sometimes helps quality without full perf loss.

sandeep: notes/action list: 1) A/B with clip98 + infra mitigations (started), 2) routing fallback & softbatch rule added, 3) compaction job enabled, 4) if clip98 still regresses >0.8% we try hybrid per-channel on top-4 layers. will post metric tables when AB completes (~6h).

ciara: thanks — ping #eng-ml-alerts if any rollback triggers. also create a small postmortem template if we end up reverting.

sandeep: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
